test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Feb, 2026 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
In the context of LPG reforms in India, the opening of the economy has led to a rapid ______.

I. increase in the foreign direct investment

II. decrease in the foreign exchange reserve
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **New Economic Policy (NEP)** launched in **1991** introduced the **LPG (Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization)** model. By dismantling the **License Raj** and allowing **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** through automatic and government routes, India became a prime destination for global capital, leading to a massive increase in foreign investment across sectors like **telecommunications**, **retail**, and **manufacturing**. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• Prior to **1991**, India faced a severe **Balance of Payments (BoP) crisis**, where **foreign exchange reserves** fell to approximately 1.2 billion USD, barely enough to cover two weeks of essential imports. The opening of the economy actually facilitated a rapid build-up of these reserves through increased **exports**, **foreign institutional investment (FII)**, and **inward remittances**, rather than a decrease. ***Hence, statement II is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **LPG Reforms** were initiated under the leadership of Prime Minister **P.V. Narasimha Rao** and Finance Minister **Dr. Manmohan Singh** to prevent a national economic collapse.

 
 
• **Liberalization**: This involved the **deregulation** of industrial sectors, allowing private businesses to expand without excessive government oversight and reducing **import tariffs**.
 
• **Privatization**: The process of **disinvestment** in **Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)** was accelerated to improve efficiency and reduce the fiscal burden on the state.
 
• **Globalization**: This aimed to integrate the Indian economy with the global market by reducing trade barriers and allowing the **Indian Rupee** to be partially convertible on the current account.
 
• **Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA)**: In 1999, **FEMA** replaced the more restrictive **FERA** to facilitate external trade and payments and promote orderly development of the foreign exchange market in India.
